title: R36 (a lone sent counterattacker auto-forms) is unmarked, but its guard was flipped to assert the opposite
summary: R36 says that when a round-2 counterattack pool holds exactly one unit and no ridable spell token, the only-unit formation is auto-declared as a forced action. On 2026-08-24 (a decisions-for-the-player audit) test 32 was flipped: its comment says the auto-declare branch is deleted, and it asserts forcedAction is null and that both attacking and declining are legal. No ruling records the reversal, and R36's heading carries no reversal mark, so the register still presents R36 as current. Register fix: write the reversing ruling (or mark R36) and point R36's heading at it.

title: 21-fixes test title claims round 2 is restricted to sent counterattackers but only tests the no-send case
summary: The test 'round 2 after a real round-1 battle still restricts to the sent counterattackers' declares blocks with no send and asserts only that the battle is over (no round 2). It never reaches a round 2 in which a unit that stayed home is refused as an attacker, so the restriction its title names is not asserted by it. The restriction is shown elsewhere only indirectly (test 32 asserts the attacker pool equals the sent unit). A guard that tries to attack in round 2 with a unit that was not sent would make the title true.
